# pki_certificate (Data Source)

Decodes a certificate — a root CA delivered from Bitwarden, an issued leaf, material adopted from another issuer — and reports its parts for inspection or assertion before building anything on top of it.

Unlike the resources of the same family, this data source does not create anything: it reads an existing certificate. The typed extension attributes (`basic_constraints`, `key_usage`, `extended_key_usage`, `name_constraints`, `san`) are parsed for convenience, and the complete `extensions` list carries every extension verbatim — including the ones the typed attributes surface — so a caller asserting on an extension the provider has no typed attribute for still has somewhere to look.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# The CA is delivered from Bitwarden into a Kubernetes Secret, so it arrives
# base64-encoded. No decoding step is needed.
data "kubernetes_secret" "ca" {
  metadata {
    name      = "pki-ca"
    namespace = "homelab-pki"
  }
}

data "pki_certificate" "ca" {
  content_base64 = data.kubernetes_secret.ca.binary_data["tls.crt"]
}

# Assert on adopted material before building anything on top of it.
check "ca_can_sign_crls" {
  assert {
    condition     = contains(data.pki_certificate.ca.key_usage.usages, "crlSign")
    error_message = "The CA cannot sign CRLs; pki_crl will fail against it."
  }
}

output "ca_expires" {
  value = data.pki_certificate.ca.not_after
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `content_base64` (String) The certificate's DER, standard base64-encoded, so material read straight out of a Kubernetes Secret needs no decoding step. Exactly one of `content_pem` and `content_base64` must be set.
- `content_pem` (String) The certificate as a PEM `CERTIFICATE` block. Exactly one of `content_pem` and `content_base64` must be set.

### Read-Only

- `authority_key_id` (String) The `authorityKeyIdentifier` extension's key identifier, lowercase hex. Null when the certificate carries no authorityKeyIdentifier — which includes every self-signed root whose issuer DN equals its subject DN, because crypto/x509 omits the extension in that case.
- `basic_constraints` (Attributes) The `basicConstraints` extension (RFC 5280 4.2.1.9), decoded. `path_len` is null when the certificate carries no `pathLenConstraint`. Null when the extension is absent. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--basic_constraints))
- `extended_key_usage` (Attributes) The `extendedKeyUsage` extension (RFC 5280 4.2.1.12), decoded. Null when the extension is absent. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--extended_key_usage))
- `extensions` (Attributes List) Every extension the certificate carries, in declaration order, each reported unparsed as `{oid, critical, value_base64}`. This is the **complete** list, including extensions the typed attributes above also surface (`basic_constraints`, `key_usage`, `extended_key_usage`, `name_constraints`, `san`, `subject_key_id`, `authority_key_id`): the typed attributes are for reading convenience, and this list is the source of truth, so a caller asserting on an extension the provider has no typed attribute for has somewhere to look without losing anything the typed path already parsed. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--extensions))
- `fingerprint_sha256` (String) The SHA-256 hash of the certificate's **DER**, lowercase hex — the certificate's identity. Distinct from `public_key_fingerprint_sha256`, which is the OpenSSH fingerprint of the public key the certificate carries: two certificates for the same key have the same `public_key_fingerprint_sha256` but different `fingerprint_sha256`.
- `is_ca` (Boolean) Whether the certificate asserts `cA: TRUE` in its `basicConstraints`. Convenience derived from `basic_constraints.ca`; null only when the certificate carries no basicConstraints at all, which is rare in practice — RFC 5280 recommends but does not require it.
- `issuer` (Attributes List) The certificate's issuer DN as a list of `{oid, value, string_type}` objects in declaration order, in the same shape as `subject`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--issuer))
- `key_usage` (Attributes) The `keyUsage` extension (RFC 5280 4.2.1.3), decoded into its RFC 5280 bit-order name list. Null when the extension is absent. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--key_usage))
- `name_constraints` (Attributes) The `nameConstraints` extension (RFC 5280 4.2.1.10), decoded. Null when the extension is absent. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--name_constraints))
- `not_after` (String) The certificate's `notAfter`, RFC 3339 timestamp.
- `not_before` (String) The certificate's `notBefore`, RFC 3339 timestamp.
- `public_key_algorithm` (String) The public key's algorithm: `RSA`, `ECDSA`, or `ED25519`.
- `public_key_fingerprint_sha256` (String) The SHA-256 fingerprint of the certificate's **public key** in OpenSSH form (`SHA256:base64`, matching `pki_private_key`'s `fingerprint_sha256`). This is **not** the certificate fingerprint: it identifies the key, not the certificate that carries it. See `fingerprint_sha256` for the certificate's own identity.
- `public_key_pem` (String) The certificate's public key, PKIX-encoded (`PUBLIC KEY`).
- `san` (Attributes) The `subjectAltName` extension, decoded into its four GeneralName types. Null when the certificate carries no subjectAltName. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--san))
- `serial_number` (String) The certificate's serial number as lowercase hex with no `0x` prefix and no leading zeros. This is the certificate's serial, not the DN attribute of the same OID-prefixed name.
- `signature_algorithm` (String) The signature algorithm the certificate carries, one of `ECDSA-SHA256`, `ECDSA-SHA384`, `ECDSA-SHA512`, `Ed25519`, `SHA256-RSA`, `SHA256-RSAPSS`, `SHA384-RSA`, `SHA384-RSAPSS`, `SHA512-RSA`, `SHA512-RSAPSS`.
- `subject` (Attributes List) The certificate's subject DN as a list of `{oid, value, string_type}` objects in declaration order — the only order a parser can report, because the DN's attribute order is part of its bytes. `string_type` is always populated, including for the `utf8` default. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--subject))
- `subject_key_id` (String) The `subjectKeyIdentifier` extension's key identifier, lowercase hex. Null when the certificate carries no subjectKeyIdentifier.
- `version` (Number) The certificate's X.509 version: `1`, `2`, or `3`.

<a id="nestedatt--basic_constraints"></a>
### Nested Schema for `basic_constraints`

Read-Only:

- `ca` (Boolean) Whether the certificate may act as a certificate authority.
- `critical` (Boolean) Whether the extension is marked critical.
- `path_len` (Number) Maximum number of intermediate CA certificates that may follow this one in a valid chain (`pathLenConstraint`). Null when the certificate carries no `pathLenConstraint`.


<a id="nestedatt--extended_key_usage"></a>
### Nested Schema for `extended_key_usage`

Read-Only:

- `critical` (Boolean) Whether the extension is marked critical.
- `usages` (List of String) Extended key usage purposes, each either a friendly name such as `clientAuth` or a dotted OID. Order is preserved, because `extendedKeyUsage` is a `SEQUENCE OF`.


<a id="nestedatt--extensions"></a>
### Nested Schema for `extensions`

Required:

- `critical` (Boolean) Whether the extension is marked critical.
- `oid` (String) Dotted-decimal OID of the extension.
- `value_base64` (String) Standard base64 of the extension's raw DER `extnValue` (the OCTET STRING content, not the whole `Extension` SEQUENCE).


<a id="nestedatt--issuer"></a>
### Nested Schema for `issuer`

Required:

- `oid` (String) Dotted-decimal OID of the DN attribute type.
- `string_type` (String) The ASN.1 string encoding of `value`: one of `utf8`, `bmp`, `ia5`, `printable`, `t61`. Always populated, including for the `utf8` default.
- `value` (String) The attribute's value.


<a id="nestedatt--key_usage"></a>
### Nested Schema for `key_usage`

Read-Only:

- `critical` (Boolean) Whether the extension is marked critical.
- `usages` (List of String) Key usage names in RFC 5280 bit order, such as `digitalSignature`, `keyEncipherment`, `keyCertSign`, and `crlSign`. The `pki_oids` data source's `key_usages` group lists every accepted name against its bit position.


<a id="nestedatt--name_constraints"></a>
### Nested Schema for `name_constraints`

Read-Only:

- `critical` (Boolean) Whether the extension is marked critical.
- `excluded_dns_domains` (List of String) Excluded DNS name subtrees.
- `excluded_email_domains` (List of String) Excluded `rfc822Name` subtrees.
- `excluded_ip_ranges` (List of String) Excluded IP address ranges, in CIDR notation.
- `excluded_uri_domains` (List of String) Excluded URI subtrees.
- `permitted_dns_domains` (List of String) Permitted DNS name subtrees.
- `permitted_email_domains` (List of String) Permitted `rfc822Name` subtrees.
- `permitted_ip_ranges` (List of String) Permitted IP address ranges, in CIDR notation.
- `permitted_uri_domains` (List of String) Permitted URI subtrees.


<a id="nestedatt--san"></a>
### Nested Schema for `san`

Read-Only:

- `critical` (Boolean) Whether the extension is marked critical.
- `dns_names` (List of String) `dNSName` entries, in declaration order.
- `email_addresses` (List of String) `rfc822Name` entries, in declaration order.
- `ip_addresses` (List of String) `iPAddress` entries as plain addresses (`10.0.0.5`, `fd00::5`), in declaration order.
- `uris` (List of String) `uniformResourceIdentifier` entries, in declaration order.


<a id="nestedatt--subject"></a>
### Nested Schema for `subject`

Required:

- `oid` (String) Dotted-decimal OID of the DN attribute type.
- `string_type` (String) The ASN.1 string encoding of `value`: one of `utf8`, `bmp`, `ia5`, `printable`, `t61`. Always populated, including for the `utf8` default.
- `value` (String) The attribute's value.
